transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Ever since all the changes at work, I feel like I’m reacting badly to everything and I can’t adjust to the new setup no matter how hard I try. I'm hoping to figure out why I'm having so much trouble coping with it all.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'reacting badly' - are you experiencing a lot of anxiety, feeling overwhelmed, or having trouble sleeping because of these work changes?

By "reacting badly," I mean I have a much shorter fuse now; a small shipping error or schedule change triggers this mix of panic, anger, and an urge to just walk out. I feel constantly on edge and overwhelmed at work, losing the steady, organized groove I used to have. Sleep isn't really the main issue, it's more about this intense emotional overwhelm during the day.
Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social or other areas of functioning outside of work, or is this emotional overwhelm primarily confined to your work environment?

It has definitely spilled over into my personal life. I've pretty much stopped doing the things I used to enjoy, like playing in my rec league basketball team and visiting museums. Now, I feel like my entire life just revolves around stressing and worrying about work.

You've mentioned feeling overwhelmed and a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you tell me if you've also experienced any feelings of worthlessness or guilt that aren't directly related to the issues at work?

No, I haven't really experienced feelings of worthlessness or guilt that are unrelated to work. Almost all of my distress and negative feelings are directly tied to the stressful changes at my job and my struggles to adapt to them.
Can you describe how your symptoms started and how long you've been experiencing them, specifically in relation to the changes at work?

I started noticing I was way more on edge and overwhelmed within a few weeks of the merger changes and rotating shifts kicking in. These struggles have been going on for about four months now, ever since the restructuring really took hold.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of emotional overwhelm, anxiety, and impaired functioning in both work and personal life, directly tied to a significant stressor (work changes), suggest an adjustment disorder. The absence of feelings of worthlessness or guilt unrelated to work and the direct link between symptoms and the stressor support this diagnosis over other possibilities like post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety disorders.
